articles.title: "Friends with benefits": Zion Williamson finally addresses relationship with se*ual assault accuser in a surprising revelation
articles.summary: NBA News: Zion Williamson has denied the allegations made by a woman who accused him of r*** and se*ual battery, describing their relationship in court document.
articles.body: Zion Williamson has denied the allegations made by a woman who accused him of r*** and se*ual battery, describing their relationship in court documents as a consensual, casual “friends with benefits” arrangement. The New Orleans Pelicans star has issued a general denial of the claims and maintains that he never harmed the woman, identified in the case as Jane Doe.The dispute stems from a civil lawsuit filed in Los Angeles that accuses Williamson of a pattern of abusive and controlling behavior during a relationship that allegedly began while he was at Duke and continued until 2023. Williamson's legal team has rejected those allegations and says the relationship was casual and ended years ago.Zion Williamson's relationship with his se*ual assault accuser revealedZion Williamson's latest position centers on his description of the relationship with Jane Doe. According to the legal documents cited in several reports, including TMZ and Daily Mail, he says the two never dated or lived together and characterized their interactions as “friendly and casual” and consensual. He also disputes the allegations of s*xual assault, battery, and domestic violence.The statement contrasts with the claims made in the lawsuit. Doe alleges that she and Williamson began dating around 2018, when he was playing at Duke, and remained together until 2023. The complaint alleges a broader pattern of physical, emotional and se*ual abuse and describes two alleged r*** incidents after Williamson moved to Beverly Hills during the COVID-19 period. Those are allegations, not established findings in the supplied material.Williamson also disputes the legal basis for some of the claims. His filings reportedly argue that California laws concerning se*ual battery, stalking and domestic violence do not apply to alleged incidents said to have occurred in North Carolina, Texas and Louisiana. He has also described the domestic violence allegation as “nonsensical,” maintaining that the pair never lived together.The case therefore involves two sharply different accounts of the relationship. Doe's complaint portrays it as a long-term relationship marked by alleged coercion and abuse, while Williamson's legal response characterizes it as consensual and casual. The supplied material does not establish the truth of either account.What did Zion Williamson's representatives say?Williamson's attorneys have consistently rejected the allegations. In a statement released in May 2026, his representatives said, “We take these allegations with the utmost seriousness, and we unequivocally deny them. The allegations contained in the complaint are categorically false and reckless.” (via Daily Mail).The statement also challenged the motive behind the lawsuit, saying, “This appears to be an attempt to exploit a professional athlete driven by a financial motive rather than any legitimate grievance.” His attorneys said Williamson and the plaintiff “never dated,” while describing their relationship as consensual and casual. “But did maintain a consensual, casual relationship that began more than six years ago, when he was 18 years old. That relationship ended years ago.”Williamson's representatives further claimed that the plaintiff began demanding millions of dollars following the end of the relationship. “Only after the friendship ended did she begin demanding millions of dollars,” the rep shared. They said Williamson reported what they described as extortion attempts to law enforcement and indicated that he intended to pursue counterclaims and damages over what they called a defamatory lawsuit.The plaintiff's attorneys have rejected that characterization. Sam Taylor of the Lanier Law Firm previously said, “We and our client do not want to litigate this case in the press,” while emphasizing the seriousness of the allegations and saying the plaintiff intended to pursue the case in court.Another attorney for Doe, Rachel Lanier, alleged a pattern of coercive control and threats. “This case shows a disturbing pattern of coercive control, threats, and domination, including stalking, strangulation and threats with a loaded firearm,” she said in the supplied material. “Mr. Williamson used his wealth and fame to isolate, silence and control my client, who only after many months of medical treatment and counseling is able to come forward and describe what she endured,” via Daily Mail.The lawsuit comes amid a turbulent period for WilliamsonThe legal dispute is another off-court issue surrounding Williamson, whose personal life has previously generated significant attention. In 2023, he and Ahkeema Love announced they were expecting a daughter. That announcement was followed by allegations from Moriah Mills, who claimed she had been romantically involved with Williamson and shared alleged private messages.The supplied material also notes that Love was arrested in April in connection with allegations involving another woman romantically linked to Williamson. Police alleged that Love threatened the woman and later attacked her at Williamson's home. The material states that Love was charged with home invasion, aggravated battery and stalking.Those incidents are separate from the civil lawsuit brought by Jane Doe. As per reports, neither woman involved in the Love case is believed to be the plaintiff in the r*** lawsuit.Lindsey Hunter said Zion Williamson needs helpWilliamson's off-court controversies have also drawn commentary from former NBA players. Former Detroit Pistons guard Lindsey Hunter and Hall of Famer Tim Hardaway previously discussed Williamson's career and personal issues, with Hunter making a strong claim about the Pelicans forward's behavior.“He got a problem,” Hunter said in an episode of Crossover Podcast. “The man’s a s*x addict. He’s been caught. He needs help.”Hunter continued, “Why does he keep texting them from his phone? He’s going for like p-rnstars. What is wrong with him? He needs to chill out. They need to give him therapy.”Hunter's comments were commentary rather than a medical diagnosis established in the supplied material. The same material says Williamson has not been involved in any newly reported off-court incidents lately and notes recent footage of him working in the gym.For Williamson, the civil case remains a significant off-court issue as he prepares for another NBA season. articles.title: LeBron James makes an update about collaborating with Mercedes Maybach to raise millions for the people in Akron
articles.summary: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, has been an important person in his hometown Akron as he has helped a number of children and families
articles.body: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, has been an important person in his hometown Akron as he has helped a number of children and families coming from underprivileged families. Ahead of his last season on the court with the Philadelphia 76ers, LeBron James’ foundation reflects on his collaboration with Mercedes Maybach for the people of AkronLeBron James’ foundation has shared an update about the NBA icon partnering with Mercedes Maybach to raise more fundsA few hours ago, the 41 year old NBA legend’s foundation, the LeBron James Family Foundation, took to social media to open up about partnering with Mercedes Maybach, the proceeds of which will be used to help people in Akron.The post read as, “The dual emblems say it all: @kingjames called the play, and Mercedes-Maybach brought it to life…This exceptional [Mercedes-Maybach S-Class] will soon be offered at auction in support of the LeBron James Family Foundation.”The post added, “It's being showcased now until the 27th of September at Mercedes-Benz Studio Los Angeles. A one-of-a-kind story, made to make a difference.”For the unversed, a few days ago, the four time NBA champion LeBron James took to his social media to share his collaboration with Mercedes-Maybach.Two custom 2027 Mercedes-Maybach S 680 sedans, with the near-identical twin of his personal vehicle are being designed. While one will be the NBA legend’s personal car, the second one will be auctioned off and the proceeds from it will directly benefit the LeBron James Family Foundation.LeBron James has remained committed to helping and being there for the people from his hometown amid his immense successOver the last two decades, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon LeBron James has collaborated with philanthropists and luxurious brands to raise millions for the people of Akron.A few years ago, in an interview with ABC News, LeBron James said, “For me, to be able to go back into my community and have hands on, start kid by kid, block by block and street by street, and building that up, I feel like that helps us to make a change, ultimately, for the rest of us…”The four time NBA champion added, “We have a lot of parents here that didn't graduate high school," James told Nichols. "So not only are we tracking our kids here to make them become better, we're also lending a helping hand to a lot of the parents that didn't graduate high school, and putting them in programs where they can get their high school diploma, and get a GED."Set up in 2004, the LeBron James Family Foundation has only expanded and changed countless lives across the state while the NBA legend has been a strong supporter.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: JJ Redick takes shot at LeBron James, promises starters will not be all 'white guys' in odd presser
articles.summary: JJ Redick made an awkward quip about his Lakers starting lineup's racial makeup while addressing the viral "Snowtime" nickname for Luka Doncic's squad.
articles.body: You can put a podcaster in the head coach's chair, but you still end up with a podcaster. Los Angeles Lakers coach JJ Redick proved as much during his annual news conference Thursday, giving answers better suited for the Twitter timeline than a head coach's seat. First, Redick offered a shady response about the team gelling after superstar LeBron James departed. LEBRON JAMES TELLS LOS ANGELES LAKERS HE WILL LEAVE IN FREE AGENCY AFTER EIGHT SEASONS: REPORT He pointedly noted that this roster has a clearer identity than past squads led by James, his former podcast co-host. "I think we’ve always tried to give our players clearly defined roles, and I think with this group, [it’s] probably the first time in my three years here that I feel like the pieces actually fit together," Redick said. "And so those roles probably get even more crystallized." Since LeBron’s departure, a running joke has taken over Lakers fandom. "Snowtime" has trended across social media as the tongue-in-cheek nickname for the Lakers' projected core of Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler — with nods to depth pieces like Dalton Knecht and Maxi Kleber. STEPHEN A SMITH SHOWS HIS PRIVILEGE BY MOCKING LAKERS' ROSTER FOR HAVING TOO MANY 'WHITE DUDES' Because the team's projected top talent isn't Black, the online gag caught fire, and Redick awkwardly addressed it with a questionable remark about his starting unit. Without much context, Redick said he was confident two positions in his lineup would "not be white." "I'm pretty confident in three of the spots," Redick said. "The other two spots will not be two white guys." It was a sarcastic wink to the online crowd, and a cheap internet laugh at best. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Redick now enters his third season at the helm in Los Angeles. His squad was swept in the Western Conference Semifinals by OKC last spring, following a first-round exit against the Minnesota Timberwolves in his inaugural season. Before taking the bench, Redick spent 15 years as an NBA sharpshooter. In 2024, he teamed up with LeBron James to co-host "Mind the Game," a wine-drinking, X's-and-O's basketball podcast. PHILADELPHIA ATHLETES, INCLUDING NEW TEAMMATES, REACT TO LEBRON JAMES JOINING 76ERS: 'WELCOME TO THE CITY' By July 2026, after two seasons together in LA, the dynamic completely shifted when LeBron packed his bags for Philly, leaving Redick to run the show solo. articles.title: Caitlin Clark Posts Career-Low, Box Score Stats, Highlights as Lynx Beat Fever in Season Finale
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever lost playoff seeding ground and Aliyah Boston to injury during Thursday night's regular-season finale.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever lost playoff seeding ground and Aliyah Boston to injury during Thursday night's regular-season finale.

The Fever will enter the postseason as the WNBA's No. 6 seed after conceding a 86-66 blowout loss to a Minnesota Lynx team missing star rookie Olivia Miles.

Clark recorded career lows in the loss with two points, no three-pointers and 8.3 percent shooting from the field.

Live WNBA Live Updates in Regular Season-Finale

Boston exited the game in the second quarter and was later ruled out with a right lower leg injury.

Here's a look at highlights from a Thursday matchup that will shape the first round of the WNBA postseason.

Shortly after Sophie Cunningham said her team needed to work on faster starts, the Fever recorded one of their slowest first halves of the season against a team that has already clinched the WNBA's top seed.

The Lynx opened scoring with a Maya Caldwell three-pointer, which Clark answered with her lone field goal of the game. The Fever went on to get outscored 21-4 in the opening minutes.

Indiana could not contain the Lynx's three-point shooting as the home team went 11-for-18 from behind the arc through twenty minutes.

The Fever, on the other hand, made three of 21 attempts from deep as the Lynx surged out to a 30-point halftime lead.

Natasha Howard and Kayla McBride had combined for more points (34) than the entirety of the Fever (32) by the break.

The Fever outscored the Lynx 25-10 in the fourth quarter but were unable to make up ground from the early deficit.

Indiana finished the game having shot 34 percent from the field and 16 percent from deep.

The Fever will now wait for an injury update on Boston while preparing to potentially start out the postseason against the defending WNBA champions.

Thursday's loss, combined with the Washington Mystics' victory over the Chicago Sky the same night, will drop the Fever in the WNBA's playoff seeding from No. 5 to No. 6.

Instead of the Atlanta Dream, Fever will now be slated to take on either the Las Vegas Aces or Golden State Valkyries when the postseason tips off this Sunday.

If the Aces claim a Thursday night win over the Phoenix Mercury, Las Vegas will secure the No. 2 seed. The Valkyries could alternatively lock in a first-round matchup against the Fever with a win over the Los Angeles Sparks or an Aces loss.

articles.title: Indiana Fever routed by Lynx in regular season finale as Caitlin Clark posts career-worst performance
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark was held to a career-worst two points on 1-of-12 shooting as the Minnesota Lynx routed the Indiana Fever 86-66 in the finale.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever flamed out in their regular-season finale. Indy stood no chance Thursday night as the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx cruised to an 86-66 beatdown. Fever fans were also watching the Lynx matchup for playoff seeding purposes. With the loss, the Fever fall into a matchup against the defending champion Las Vegas Aces, led by MVP frontrunner A'ja Wilson. With a win, Indiana could have faced the Atlanta Dream. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! On Tuesday, Indy faced the Lynx at home and pulled off a statement win, at one point handing Minnesota its biggest deficit of the season. Minnesota extinguished all of Indiana's momentum in the rematch, locking down Caitlin Clark to a career-worst two points on 1-of-12 shooting (1-for-8 at halftime) in 18 minutes of action. The Fever went into the half down 62-32. Minnesota was shorthanded for a second consecutive game with rookie sensation Olivia Miles out again with a calf injury. CAITLIN CLARK RETURNS AFTER FIBA TITLE AS KELSEY MITCHELL SETS WNBA SCORING MARK IN FEVER VICTORY OVER TEMPO The Lynx rested their starters for the bulk of Tuesday's second half. Indiana seemingly followed suit on Thursday after falling behind by 30 in the third quarter, limiting Clark's floor time and seeing Sophie Cunningham held scoreless across 16 minutes. Clark had the opportunity to become the WNBA's first player to reach 900 points and 300 assists in a single season. She entered Thursday's game just 11 points shy of the 900-point mark, but fell short, finishing with two points, three assists, and four rebounds. Indiana's loss was made worse when starting center Aliyah Boston was ruled out with a right lower leg injury. The Fever also lost guard Ty Harris, who was carried off the court. On the bright side for Indy, Kelsey Mitchell broke the single-season three-pointer record, hitting her 135th of the season to pass Rhyne Howard (134). Mitchell led the team with 10 points on the night, though she snapped her streak of consecutive games with 20-plus points, ending her run at 27 games as Indiana finishes the regular season at 28-15. articles.title: Caitlin Clark's Season Box Score Stats After Final Fever Game, Where Star Ranks Among WNBA Leaders?
articles.summary: Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark's third WNBA regular season is over, and her final stats are in.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark's third WNBA regular season is over, and her final stats are in.

Clark's 22.3 points per game ranked third in the WNBA, and her 8.3 assists landed second.

Caitlin Clark posts career low in blowout loss

The former Iowa star entered Thursday scorching hot, posting 30.2 points and 10.0 assists per contest over her final five games.

She (and the rest of the starters) played limited minutes on Thursday in their loss to the first-place Minnesota Lynx.

Clark had a rough shooting night (1-of-12, two points) in an 86-66 loss, but it's full steam ahead to the playoffs for No. 6 seed Indiana with a first-round date against the No. 3 seed Las Vegas Aces.

Indiana reached the WNBA semifinals last year despite dealing with a litany of injuries, including season-ending ailments to Clark, who played just 13 regular season games and missed the playoffs.

Clark is healthy and ready to go for the playoffs, though, as Indiana searches for its first championship since 2012 and second overall.

articles.title: Los Lakers defienden su honestidad en la salida de LeBron James y la definen como "amistosa"
articles.standfirst: Rob Pelinka analiza la salida de LeBron James de los Lakers tras ocho temporadas y un anillo de campeón
articles.summary: Rob Pelinka analiza la salida de LeBron James de los Lakers tras ocho temporadas y un anillo de campeón
articles.body: El director general de los Los Angeles Lakers, Rob Pelinka, aseguró que la salida de LeBron James de la franquicia este verano fue "amistosa" y se mostró agradecido por el tiempo que el jugador pasó en el equipo. "Estoy muy agradecido por la relación que tuvimos, que se prolongó hasta este verano, cuando se tomó la decisión de que jugara en otro equipo. Se hizo de manera amistosa, profesional y elegante", aseguró Pelinka en una rueda de prensa. Tras ocho temporadas en Los Ángeles, donde ganó el anillo en 2020, James, de 41 años, firmó este verano para las dos próximas campañas con los Philadelphia 76ers. "Estamos agradecidos por la era de LeBron. Las comunicaciones con él durante este verano se llevaron a cabo de forma diplomática, profesional y honesta", añadió Pelinka. "Vimos todo esto con gratitud, porque ha sido una época increíble para nosotros aquí", insistió el directivo. James anunció el 24 de julio su decisión de fichar por los 76ers después de reconocer que, al final de la temporada pasada, llegó a pensar que se iba a retirar. "Esta es mi última decisión. No lo hago por dinero. No lo hago por mi familia. ¿Por qué sigo jugando a estas alturas? Todavía quiero sacrificarme. Todavía quiero trabajar. Todavía quiero esforzarme. Todavía quiero competir y tener la oportunidad de volver a sentir lo que es ganar", afirmó entonces James.

articles.title: Aces overwhelm Mercury for momentum heading into playoff rematch
articles.summary: PHOENIX—Closing out the year with one rematch from last year’s playoff, the Las Vegas Aces now find themselves preparing for battle against another formerly...
articles.body:
PHOENIX—Closing out the year with one rematch from last year's playoff, the Las Vegas Aces now find themselves preparing for battle against another formerly vanquished foe.

On Thursday, the Aces closed out the regular season with a bang, with A'ja Wilson and Chelsea Gray hitting double-doubles in a 100-82 victory over the Phoenix Mercury .

The win puts the Aces at seven straight to end the year, pushing them into the playoffs with serious momentum by their side once again.

Wilson put an exclamation point on her case for her fifth MVP award, securing 34 points and 10 rebounds as well as four assists and a steal. The performance guarantees that Wilson secures over 26 points per game for the second time in her career, the only player in WNBA history to reach that mark even once. Gray would also end the regular season with a strong effort, putting up 12 points while adding ten assists and five steals to continue providing value on both ends of the court.

Even Jackie Young , despite having a cold scoring night with only five points, made her presence felt elsewhere with a game-high 11 assists, seven rebounds and three steals.

However, Young's struggles to generate points made the other developments of the game so much more important for the Aces.

Stephanie Talbot , who has spent the season trying to find her fit in Las Vegas , appears to have turned the corner and is getting hot at the right time. The Aussie wing has returned from the World Cup with a vengeance, putting up 14 points, four rebounds and two steals.

"We've had 44 games to kind of work on our chemistry and figure each other out and hopefully it's all coming together at the right time," said Talbot. "Coming into playoffs, everyone's feeling good, so it's exciting."

Meanwhile, Jewell Loyd appears to have flipped a switch at the right time, providing microwave scoring with 25 points in as many minutes. This includes a game-high five three-point shots, which was more than the rest of the Aces put together.

"I think we've been stacking games together," said Loyd about the Aces' depth coming through at the right time. "Whether it's Steph coming in, Mai [Yamamoto], Cheyenne [Parker-Tyus], I think that's the job is to try to find energy on both sides of the floor.

We want to use this momentum to hopefully push us to the end and, when we play together, remember when we're excited for each other. I think that's how we play. It's just better basketball that way."

It was an important game for solutions to be found, as the Aces find themselves looking at a stern test for the first round of the WNBA playoffs.

By virtue of the Minnesota Lynx blowing out the Indiana Fever and the Golden State Valkyries roaring back against the Los Angeles Sparks to secure the second seed, the Aces get a semifinals rematch against the Fever to kickstart the journey for their fourth title in five years. Making the matchup all the more compelling is the added element of Caitlin Clark , who missed last year's playoffs due to injury. Needless to say, the Aces' path towards cementing themselves as a dynasty will not be easy.

"Obviously, they have a high-powered offense, so that's job number one is slowing them up a little bit. Easier said than done," said Aces head coach Becky Hammon about the Fever. "It's going to be a tall task for us but, coming in, we know that defense is a game changer and we're going to need a lot of it against them."

The series, as well as the WNBA playoffs, tip off on Sunday. Game One will take place at Michelob ULTRA Arena at a time to be determined.

articles.title: ‘Didn’t Do That for Caitlin (Clark),’ ‘Fire This Fool’ — Outrage Erupts As Stephanie White Reps Kelsey Mitchell Shirt at Fever’s Regular-Season Finale
articles.summary: Nothing went Caitlin Clark’s way during the Indiana Fever’s regular-season finale against the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx on Thursday. The three-time WNBA All-...
articles.body:
Nothing went Caitlin Clark 's way during the Indiana Fever 's regular-season finale against the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx on Thursday. The three-time WNBA All-Star recorded a career-low 2 points on woefully inefficient 1-for-12 shooting in the 86-66 blowout loss.

Clark didn't seem to get much support from the sideline either, as coach Stephanie White appeared in a Kelsey Mitchell Slam shirt. Clark's fanbase was furious over the lack of similar support from coach White for the WNBA superstar.

Caitlin Clark Fans Furious Over Stephanie White Wearing Kelsey Mitchell Shirt

Clark had the chance to add another record to her name. She could have become the first point guard in WNBA history to post 900 points in a single season. She was only 11 points shy. Instead, she fizzled out with her lowest-scoring game ever.

Mitchell, on the other hand, added another piece of history to her résumé. With two made 3-pointers on 6 attempts, she broke the WNBA single-season record with 135 triples.

Mitchell has been a reliable scorer throughout the 2026 season, posting a team-high 24.7 points per game. However, the four-time WNBA All-Star saw her historic 27-game 20-point streak end as she scored only 10 points against the Lynx in the final outing of the season.

Still, White in a Mitchell shirt didn't sit well with Clark supporters, who didn't hold back from digging into the Fever coach with pointed jabs.

"Stephanie White and the coaching staff wearing Kelsey Mitchell Slam shirts but didn't do that for Caitlin's Slam Kicks cover for her highly anticipated Nike shoes. Very on brand for this staff," one fan wrote .

"Stephanie White is doing everything she can to hype KM for MVP over Caitlin Clark, when Caitlin has broken so many records…KM isn't [expletive] without Caitlin Clark assisting her on her shots," another added .

"Stephanie White always reppin her fav!" one Clark loyalist asserted , arguing that White frequently shows more support for Mitchell than Clark.

Amid Clark and Mitchell's lackluster production, the Fever were run out of the building by the Lynx's relentless offense. They suffered their biggest defeat of the season.

Putting Indiana's plight in context, one X user wrote , "And look how the game is going."

"Nope NEVER! Fire this fool," another X user wrote .

Meanwhile, a few supporters believed the shirt pointed to a bigger divide within the Fever, with one asserting , "The whole coaching staff is wearing a KM shirt. They're showing they're united and F CC. I have never seen something so aggressive from a staff."

The criticism did not stop there, as a fan bluntly declared , "I legitimately despise Steph White. She is the worst thing to ever happen to the Fever. She's a bad coach and a worse human being."

While the Mitchell Slam shirt became a talking point, the bigger story is that the Lynx steamrolled the Fever with a 20-point win, sapping their momentum right before the playoffs.

The loss dropped Indiana to the No. 6 seed at 28-16. The Fever will now face the No. 3-seeded Las Vegas Aces in the first round, with the series set to begin Sunday.

The only relief for the Fever might be the fact that they won the regular-season series against Las Vegas 2-1, including both road matchups.

Still, Clark will have to put the disappointing regular-season finale behind her quickly. The Fever will need Clark at her best to stand a chance against the defending WNBA champions in Round 1 of the 2026 playoffs.
